method: Google autocomplete scrape (automation-lab/google-trends... no: automation-lab/google-autocomplete-scraper) plus Google Keyword Planner search volume (aitorsm/keyword-volume). Google Trends was attempted first but the browser scraper was IP-blocked and timed out twice; the browserless Trends actor returned unusable 1-day, independently-scaled data. Autocomplete + Keyword Planner used instead.

autocomplete.note: Rung counts sum to 1,626. They reflect the variety of distinct autocomplete questions per stage, not search frequency, and are influenced by the number of seeds per rung (3 / 2 / 4). Origin curiosity is the largest cluster.
autocomplete.originSpecificity: 43% of origin-rung suggestions (368 of 858 unique) name a specific region or grape (Barolo, Bordeaux, Burgundy, Rioja, etc.).

keywordPlanner.source: Google Keyword Planner real monthly search volume. Global (worldwide) figures are used in the visual; US figures kept for reference.

queries: how to drink wine for the first time
how to choose the right wine
what does off dry wine mean
how to taste and describe wine
how to taste wine like a sommelier
what grape is grown in burgundy

keywordPlanner.note: Rung numbers in the visual are the combined monthly GLOBAL search volume of the five example questions shown in each rung. Trend is monotonic: rung1 ~2,830, rung2 ~4,220, rung3 ~22,790, summing to ~30,000 (the headline). Rung 3 is heavily lifted by the broad query 'wine regions of france' (~22,200 global), which is itself the finding: origin curiosity commands the most search interest. Keyword Planner volumes are bucketed estimates; displayed values rounded to the nearest hundred.

headlineStats: 75% find the rules of wine intimidating (OnePoll 2022)
43% of origin searches name a specific region or grape (autocomplete)
~30,000 combined monthly global searches across these questions
usedInVisual.calloutInsight: Once the basics click, the desire to learn a wine's origin is close to universal, drawing by far the most searches. This reinforces the overall message that curiosity about the story, not price or rules, is what drives progression.
